replies.text:
Step 2 checks:
- Automated abuse of anything reachable: design says "accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it" — no sign-in, no email/SMS, no sign-up, but arbitrary outbound fetching makes it scriptable as a forward proxy against third parties and runs up our egress. Listed DoS threat 4 only covers self-inflicted memory/CPU from oversized images, not abuse of third parties from our IPs → not covered.
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing other people's content: nothing in the design names any such screen → not applicable.
- Delete/moderate/refund/approve/role-change/money with no record: the design describes only download-resize-return; no such action stated → not applicable.
- Personal/financial documents cached by browsers, proxies or CDNs: design states only that the service "resizes it and returns it"; no cache, CDN or personal data is stated → not applicable (the single-reviewer caching item depends on a cache that the design never mentions).
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV, emails, headers or another interpreter: no logging, export or email is stated in the design → not applicable.
- Single-reviewer items reviewed: decoder-exploit items (2 of them) depend on which image library is used, not on stated design; error/timing scanning and non-image echo are narrower cases of the agreed internal-read threats; internal write-via-scheme is covered by agreed threats 2 and 6; caching not stated. Only the open-proxy item is a genuinely different harm.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["image resize service", "URL fetcher", "image resizer"],
    "dataStores": ["internal databases"],
    "externalServices": ["arbitrary attacker-supplied URLs", "internal metadata service"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["VPC egress to the internet", "caller to resize service"],
    "dataClasses": [],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Service works as an open forward proxy: attackers scrape or flood third parties from our egress IPs",
      "scenario": "Any internal caller (including a compromised low-value workload) scripts the endpoint with thousands of third-party URLs. The service downloads each one and returns the body, so it becomes a free anonymising proxy: the attacker scrapes a paywalled or rate-limited site, or floods a victim host. All traffic and abuse complaints come from our egress addresses, our IP range gets blocklisted and our outbound bandwidth and egress bill climb. Harm is to our reputation and availability, distinct from the memory exhaustion threat already listed.",
      "component": "image resize service URL fetcher (egress)",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "availability" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The image service accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it." },
        { "quote": "It runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V12.6.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918", "CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because the service downloads any URL it is given, someone can use it to hammer or scrape other websites, and the complaints and blocklisting land on our own IP addresses.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict and rate-limit outbound fetches",
        "given": "an authenticated caller invoking the image resize endpoint",
        "when": "they submit URLs at high volume or for destinations outside the approved image-host allowlist",
        "then": "the service rejects non-allowlisted destinations, enforces a per-caller rate and concurrency limit on outbound fetches, and records the fetched host for abuse investigation"
      }
    }
  ]
}
